overview: From 2026-10-29 to 2026-10-30, ethereum-optimism/optimism had 3 new PRs (1 merged), 1 new issues, and 5 active contributors.

topIssues.title: kona-node: fix trust-rpc flags and match op-node defaults
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
Kona-node should continue to support configuring RPC trust. Fix the existing flags so they behave as expected, including explicitly disabling trust from the command line.

Both `--l1.trust-rpc` and `--l2.trust-rpc` default to `true`, but are plain clap boolean flags and reject `=false`. For example, `--l1.trust-rpc=false` fails with an unexpected-value error even though the help text describes behavior when the value is false. The corresponding environment variables can already select false.

Acceptance criteria:
- Both flags accept explicit `=false` and `=true` values.
- Match op-node defaults: L1 RPC trust defaults to `false`, and L2 engine RPC trust defaults to `true`. Preserve bare flags as an explicit request to enable trust (`true`).
- Preserve `KONA_NODE_L1_TRUST_RPC` and `KONA_NODE_L2_TRUST_RPC` support, with explicit CLI values taking precedence.
- Add regression coverage for both flags and their configuration behavior.

Replaces the configuration portion of #23037. The separate L1/L2 block-body and receipt verification work remains tracked in https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/446.

topIssues.title: op-deployer: interop and super-root games still gated by devFeatureBitmap in v0.9.0-dev-test.2
topIssues.author: jelias2
topIssues.body:
## Expectation

With the v0.9.0 contracts, interop and super-root games are part of the release. A fresh deployment should therefore not need `devFeatureBitmap` bits `0x1` (`OPTIMISM_PORTAL_INTEROP`) and `0x10000000` (`SUPER_ROOT_GAMES_MIGRATION`) in `globalDeployOverrides`.

The `op-deployer/v0.9.0-dev-test.1` changelog also says: "devfeatures: Enable super root games migration by default (#21689)".

## Actual

All of the following is at tag `op-deployer/v0.9.0-dev-test.2`:

- `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/pipeline/l2genesis.go`: `buildDevFeatureBitmap` returns `interop feature in devFeatureBitmap does not match the UseInterop intent flag` when `useInterop=true` and bit `0x1` is absent.
- `packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/L2Genesis.s.sol` still gates `CrossL2Inbox`, `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger`, `ETHLiquidity`, `SuperchainETHBridge` and `UndeliveredMessageExporter` on `OPTIMISM_PORTAL_INTEROP` (`Predeploys.assertGates`).
- `packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/deploy/DeployImplementations.s.sol` only deploys the `SuperFaultDisputeGame` / `SuperPermissionedDisputeGame` implementations when either bit is set, and asserts they are absent otherwise.
- `OPContractsManagerV2.sol` (around line 753) reads `isDevFeatureEnabled(SUPER_ROOT_GAMES_MIGRATION)` to decide super-root mode in `deploy`; `OPContractsManagerStandardValidator.sol` (around line 951) does the same.

Net effect: without `0x10000000`, an interop chain cannot be deployed with `respectedGameType` 5 or 9 at genesis.

## Impact

- Devnet tooling (netchef in `devnets-private`) must keep passing both bits for every interop / super-root network.
- A user who reads "interop is included" in v0.9.0 and omits the bitmap gets a late failure at L2 genesis, after the L1 contracts have already been broadcast, or a non-interop genesis if the check is bypassed.
- Example network: devnets-private PR #2317 (`int-sr-0`).

## Ask

Either:

1. Default these two bits on (or remove the gates) in op-deployer v0.9.0, so an intent with `useInterop=true` deploys the interop predeploys and super-root games without a bitmap; or
2. Document in the v0.9.0 release notes that the bitmap remains required, and which bits.

---
Filed by Claude Code on behalf of jelias2

topPRs.title: docs: add ZK proofs documentation
topPRs.author: pauldowman
topPRs.body:
Adds public docs for the ZK proof system, which is replacing Cannon-based fault proofs, so operators and readers have docs before ZK proofs ship.

- New "ZK Proofs" section under How the protocol works: hub, explainer, ZK dispute game, proof system, components, security, and reference.
- Operator pages: configuring op-zk-proposer and op-challenger for ZK games, verifying a ZK absolute prestate, and migrating a chain to ZK proofs via `opcm.upgrade`.
- An op-zk-proposer component page, a ZK section in the op-dispute-mon monitoring docs, and a shared "experimental" warning snippet.

Open items, marked as TODO comments in the pages:

- Standard values for `maxChallengeDuration`, `maxProveDuration`, `challengerBond`, and the init bond.
- The op-contracts release and superchain-ops template that support the ZK game.
- The op-zk-proposer image name and tag format.
- Adding op-zk-proposer to the component reference and release notes generators.
- Local prover support. The proposer currently proves only through the Succinct Prover Network.

The spec's `ZKDisputeGameConfig` includes a `verifier` field, but the OPCM struct doesn't: OPCM supplies its own `SP1PlonkAdapter`. These docs follow the code.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/proofs-team/issues/3

topPRs.title: kona-disc,kona-rpc!: Honor --p2p.no-discovery
topPRs.author: aakoshh
topPRs.body:
**What**

`--p2p.no-discovery` now turns discovery off. Without it, kona-node binds no UDP port, publishes no ENR, ignores its bootnodes, and connects only to its static peers, the peers that dial it, and the peers added with `opp2p_connectPeer`.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/23702

**Why**

The flag was parsed but never read: discovery always ran, bound its UDP port and published the node's ENR. With static peers (#23726), turning discovery off is how an operator keeps a node such as a sequencer off the public network. Static peers alone can't do that on a chain with built-in bootnodes, which discovery bootstraps from even with no bootnodes configured, as raised in https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23726#discussion_r4405491249.

What operators see:
- With the flag, the UDP port isn't checked at startup, so the node starts even if it's taken. Each port is now checked on its own: a port of `0` used to skip both checks.
- With discovery off, the node warns at startup if no static peers are set, and if bootnodes are set, since it ignores them.
- The P2P RPC answers as op-node's does without discovery: `opp2p_self` has no ENR, `opp2p_peerStats` has a `table` of `0`, and `opp2p_discoveryTable` returns the error `discovery disabled`. `opp2p_peerCount` returns `null` for `connectedDiscovery`. op-conductor's health check reads `peerStats.connected`, which counts static peers.
- The P2P RPC's internal errors are logged as warnings and say what failed, such as `peer_count: discovery service stopped`, where clients got a bare "Internal error" and the log had nothing. One warning's log target moved from `p2p_rpc` to `p2p::rpc`.
- `opp2p_self`'s `nodeID` comes from the peer ID, as op-node's does, not from the ENR. Both come from the same key, so the value is unchanged.
- op-devstack already starts kona-node with `KONA_NODE_P2P_NO_DISCOVERY=true` (`op-devstack/sysgo/l2_cl_kona_config.go`), which kona ignored until now. kona nodes in the acceptance tests now really run without discovery. The harnesses connect peers with `opp2p_connectPeer`, so nothing should break, but the acceptance jobs on this PR are the first to run that way.

**How**

- Disabled discovery is a state of its own, not a dummy: `NetworkHandler.discovery` is an `Option<RunningDiscovery>` that holds the discovery handler and its ENR receiver together, and without it the network actor's ENR branch never completes. A discovery that runs and then stops is still fatal, as in op-node and since #23610.
- Discovery isn't even built when it's off, because `Discv5Builder::build` binds the UDP socket itself when the listen port is `0`.
- `Discv5Handler`'s requests are now `async`, and fail with `DiscoveryStopped`. Each one used to spawn a task just to send the request, which lost the caller's tracing span.
- The docs gain a "Running without discovery" section, marked unreleased, with a table of how discovery, bootnodes and static peers combine.

**Caveats**

- The tests that discovery stays off run offline against local nodes: the node leaves its UDP port free, also on OP Mainnet's chain ID, which has built-in bootnodes; it doesn't answer a discovery node that has it as a bootnode; it never reaches the bootnodes it's given; and it starts with its UDP port taken. Each fails if discovery runs, which I checked by forcing it on.
- A test that a node without discovery connects to no extra peers on OP Sepolia couldn't tell whether discovery ran: with discovery on and network access, the node found 34 nodes in 15 s but dialed none, probably because they're on other OP chains (not verified). So it isn't included.

**Alternatives**

- A noop discovery task that answers requests from an unstarted `Discv5`, as #23035 did. It needs a dummy ENR sender kept alive, `opp2p_self` would advertise an ENR whose UDP port nobody serves, and "disabled" would look the same as "found nobody".
- An empty list from `opp2p_discoveryTable`, as the issue first suggested. op-node returns the error, so kona does too.
- Reviews run: `rust-code-reviewer`, `deletion-reviewer`, and a general correctness, security and docs review. Dismissed findings: the CLI port test frees a TCP port and then reuses it, a small window that's common in tests; the rest are listed as potential follow-ups.

**Potential follow-ups**

- Rename the network types: `Discv5Driver` and `NetworkDriver` are unstarted, `GossipDriver` is live, `Discv5Handler` is a client of a task, and `NetworkHandler` is the actor's live state.
- `kona-node net` exits right after starting when its RPC server is disabled, since `OptionFuture::from(None)` resolves at once (not verified by running). It also logs `Discovery=0` without discovery, and keeps serving RPC after its network actor stops.
- A `discovery_enabled` label on the CLI metrics gauge, so dashboards can tell disabled discovery from an empty table.
- `opp2p_peers` decodes peer IDs into node IDs by hand, duplicating `kona_peers::peer_id_to_node_id`.
- `HandlerRequest::Metrics` is only used by the discovery example, and `Discv5::metrics()` reads process-wide counters without the driver, so the request could go.
- Warn about other discovery flags that go unused without discovery, such as `--p2p.bootstore` and `--p2p.discovery.interval`.
- The ENR and chain ID checks in `rust/kona/tests/node/common/rpc_test.go` can no longer fire in devstack, and comments there are stale.
- Not verified: the built-in OP Mainnet bootnode ENRs may carry other chains' IDs, which `EnrValidation` drops.

BREAKING CHANGE: Operators who already set `--p2p.no-discovery` or `KONA_NODE_P2P_NO_DISCOVERY=true` now get a node without discovery; remove the flag to keep it. For Rust users: `kona_disc::Discv5Handler`'s request methods are `async` and return `Result<_, DiscoveryStopped>`, so await them in place of the receiver they returned. `kona_rpc::P2pRpc::new` takes an `Option<Discv5Handler>` and the chain ID. `kona_node_service::NetworkConfig` has a new `discovery_enabled` field; set it to `true` to keep discovery. `NetworkDriver.discovery` and `NetworkHandler.discovery` are `Option`s, and `NetworkHandler.enr_receiver` moved into `RunningDiscovery`.

topPRs.title: op-node: log on SystemConfig update events
topPRs.author: arifrhm
topPRs.body:
### Description

When `op-node` processes `SystemConfig` update events from L1 receipts in `ProcessSystemConfigUpdateLogEvent`, it previously did so silently. This PR adds structured log messages for each event type so node operators and monitoring systems can track governance and system configuration updates directly in `op-node` logs.

### Changes
- Updated `ProcessSystemConfigUpdateLogEvent` and `UpdateSystemConfigWithL1Receipts` in `op-node/rollup/derive/system_config.go` to accept a `log.Logger` (nil-safe).
- Added structured `Info` logs for all 8 update event types:
  - Batcher address (`batcher`)
  - Fee scalars (`overhead`, `scalar`, and Ecotone single-scalar format)
  - Gas limit (`gasLimit`)
  - EIP-1559 parameters (`params`)
  - Operator fee parameters (`params`)
  - Min base fee (`minBaseFee`)
  - DA footprint gas scalar (`daFootprintGasScalar`)
  - Unsafe block signer (noted as ignored in derivation)
- Threaded the derivation pipeline's logger from `L1Traversal` in `l1_traversal.go`.
- Added `TestProcessSystemConfigUpdateLogEvent_Logging` in `system_config_test.go` using `testlog.CaptureLogger` to assert log message emission for every event type.

Fixes #12974

topPRs.title: kona-node!: fix RPC trust flags and match op-node defaults
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Operators can explicitly configure L1 and L2 RPC trust with `=false` or `=true`; previously these CLI values were rejected. Kona now matches op-node defaults: L1 RPC trust is `false`, and L2 engine RPC trust remains `true`. Bare flags enable trust, and explicit CLI values take precedence over environment settings.

BREAKING CHANGE: Operators who relied on the previous L1 trust default now get block hash verification. Set `--l1.trust-rpc=true` or `KONA_NODE_L1_TRUST_RPC=true` to retain the previous behavior.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/23688. Provider verification changes remain tracked in https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/446.

All 103 kona-node tests and full workspace lint pass locally.

CI: required Rust and Rust end-to-end gates pass. The Go suite fails in the unchanged `op-deployer` fork-upgrade test `TestEndToEndBootstrapApplyWithUpgrade/opcm_upgrade_test/run_past_upgrades`, which panics in `script.Host.onExit` with `index out of range [-1]` ([job output](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5776037)). This test runs Go’s contract-deployment host and does not start Kona.
